title.narrative: Heilongjiang Cold Weather Smart Public Transportation System

description.narrative: The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to upgrade the quality and efficiency of public transport services in selected public transport corridors of the project cities.

The objective of the Heilongjiang Cold Weather Smart Public Transport System Project for China is to upgrade the quality and efficiency of public transport services in selected public transport corridors of the project cities. The project has five components. (1) Public transport corridor improvement component will finance the improvement of three designated public transport corridors in Harbin and five in Mudanjiang by: (a) improving pavement conditions and developing new lane configurations within the current pavement width to provide dedicated bus-priority lanes, bike lanes, and pedestrian facilities; (b) installing bus stops and providing heated indoor bus waiting facilities, limited underground conduit/pipeline, sidewalk and roadside parking improvement. (2) The second component is the public transport infrastructure improvement. (3) Traffic management and safety improvement component will finance the procurement of equipment and related civil works for traffic management in Harbin and Mudanjiang for: (1) traffic control system, including traffic signals with bus priority function to ensure bus priority and pedestrian crossings safety; (2) traffic monitoring and violation detection system; (3) real time traffic information system and traffic guidance system; and (4) traffic safety education. (4) Emergency response and road maintenance component will support Harbin in the development of an effective emergency response and road maintenance system. (5) Capacity building component will support improvements to the institutional and financing framework within which public transport services are developed and operated in both Harbin and Mudanjiang.

Increased annual bus ridership volume along the targeted corridors. (Million/year) (Harbin)

comment.narrative:
<p>The annual bus ridership volume along the targeted corridors increased by 18.64% and did not reach the intended targte of 35%.</p>
<p>The impact of COVID on the ridership on public transport in China and in both cities have been important. Second, as highlighted in Harbin National ICR, total population of Harbin has steadily declined since 2014, and the population in 2018 was only 96.4% of the 2014 population reducing the number of travelers. The construction of Harbin subway and the increased use of shared bicycles in Harbin have also adversely affected the use of public transportation in the city. </p>

Number of passenger hubs and depots constructed. (Mudanjiang)

comment.narrative:
<p>As per the ISR of June 2021, and the commitment letter annexed to the Aide Memoire of April 2021 mission, Mudanjiang, was finalizing the construction of Huanlin Bus Depot which was almost completed in June 2021, and Daqing bus maintenance facility which hasn’t yet started construction works due to issues in land acquisition.</p>

<p>In December 2021, the counterparts confirmed the completion of Hualin Bus Depot and the beginning of the construction of Daqing bus depot. A letter has been received by the Bank, committing to complete Daqing bud depot by June 2022.</p>

<p>This target has not been met. </p>

comment.narrative:
<p>The baseline and target are for the five corridors originally planned, while one was dropped (6.6 km dropped out of 25.3 kmtotal). As no disaggregated data is available, these are maintained for evaluation.</p>
<p>The bus speed has increased in Mudanjiang from its baselines value at 19.1 km/hour to its target of 24 km/hour (as per the Mudanjiang ICR of November 2021).</p>

<p>The baseline and target should have been adjusted at restructuring. The data for 2015 for the new corridors have been consideredas the new baseline for evaluation. <strong><u>The baseline for this indicator shall be 28.</u></strong></p>
<p>The bus speed has increased in Harbin to reach its intended target from the adjusted baseline of 28 km/hour to 34.1 km/hour.</p>

title.narrative: Reduced fatalities and major injuries along the targeted corridors (Mudanjiang)

comment.narrative:
<p>The baseline and target are for the five corridors originally planned, while one was dropped (6.6 km dropped out of 25.3 kmtotal). As the baseline is cumulative for the 5 corridors, and no disaggregated data is available, the baseline has been adjusted on a prorata basis, reducing the baseline from 32 cases per year to 26 cases per year.</p>
<p>The number of fatalities and major injuries has decreased from the adjusted baseline of 26 to 10 in June 2020, reaching 0 in June 2021 – no fatalities or major injuries identified from January to June 2021, as compared to the original target of 20 fatalities or major injuries. The number for fatalities and major injuries for the full year of 2020 is 5.</p>
